meal.title: Printing variables with format specifiers
meal.objective: Use printf format specifiers to display variable values

voice.script: Ever wondered how a program turns numbers into readable text? How do you show the value of a variable on the screen? In C, the percent sign inside a text pattern tells printf where to insert a variable. %d stands for a whole number, %s stands for a sequence of characters, %f stands for a floating point number, and %c stands for a single character. %s is basically going to allow us to include some text. Here is the complete program. It declares an integer called age, a string called name, a floating point called gpa, and a character called grade. Then it calls printf four times, each time using the matching specifier. Running it prints each variable with its proper specifier. The output shows the integer, the string, the float, and the character. Remember each specifier matches a specific type of data. Try printing your own variables using different specifiers.
